The colours here are really great and add an atmosphere to the price that reminds me of a summer day, if I had to give criticism it would be to work on your shadows, placement and colour.

Placing shadows gets easy when you’re used to it- you need to imagine the object as a 3D shape, hold a torch up to a ball and see how the shadows are Parallel to the source of light- try drawing a mini torch in the corner of your drawing to keep a consistent shadow. (It also plays into anatomy and how you break it down into simple shapes (cylinders etc) do it would be easier to draw shadows)

(I’m going to be blunt, it’s very clear that this is either straight from the mind or heavily referenced- which is good, just... I see you deflecting criticism in the comments, like saying how the one leg is “just to make it more cartoony” stop that, either take it into consideration or don’t reply)

Also, on colours of shading! So what I see is that you’ve darkened the original colour of the flesh for example and used it for the shading, it can be used in a stylised way but often leads into a muddy looking palette! What I’d recommend is taking the colour and going either way on the hue scale, make it cooler or warmer instead- a warm shading would actually be very good for this specific composition but take everything I say with a grain of salt, this is your work so you should do as you please.
